title: Meet Sentinel-2

cues.text: Now that you understand the basics of satellite imagery, let’s meet Sentinel-2.
Sentinel-2 is part of the European Union’s Copernicus Earth observation programme.
The mission uses optical instruments to collect information about Earth’s land and coastal areas.
Its observations are useful for studying vegetation, land cover, agriculture, water bodies, and changes in settlements.
Sentinel-2 measures reflected energy in several spectral bands.
Some bands have ten-metre spatial resolution, while others have twenty-metre or sixty-metre resolution.
The available detail therefore depends on the band you are using.
The Sentinel-2 mission uses two satellites working together to provide frequent observations.
Under favourable conditions, the combined mission can revisit a location approximately every five days, although actual usable observations depend on location, cloud cover, and other conditions.
Clouds are an important limitation for optical imagery because they can obscure the surface.
Scientists often use cloud masks and other quality checks before analysing an image.
As you explore LumosX, remember that satellite images are measurements collected for scientific purposes, not simply photographs from space.
